The timing of smoking bans in restaurants varies significantly by country and US state, making this a question with multiple valid answers depending on jurisdiction. In the United States, Minnesota was the first state to restrict smoking in public spaces including restaurants in 1975, though it initially only required designated "No Smoking" sections rather than a full ban [d6]. California became the first US state to fully ban smoking in restaurants in 1995, with bars added to the ban in 1998 [d1][d7]. Utah also banned smoking specifically in restaurants effective 1995, though its ban did not extend to worksites and bars until 2009 [d9]. At the comprehensive state level, Delaware was the first US state to implement a complete smoke-free law covering workplaces, restaurants, and bars in 2002, followed by New York in 2003 and Massachusetts in 2004 [d9]. In the late 1990s and early 2000s, more states began adopting broad smoking bans covering restaurants [d3]. Internationally, India introduced a law banning smoking in public places including restaurants in 2003 [d6], while Ireland became the first country to ban smoking in all enclosed public spaces in 2004 [d8].
